## v1.11.0 — Gemini thought signature channels, automatic preset updates, switches in user modules

### Gemini thought signatures
- `connection.sendThoughtSignature` now picks a **channel**: `false` (off, default) / `vertex` / `aistudio` (`true` = `vertex`). A signature only validates on the backend that issued it, so the channel comes from the configuration and is never guessed from ST's API connection: users often go through routers and reverse proxies.
- `syntheticTurns[].thoughtSignature` holds one signature per channel (`{ vertex, aistudio }`); a plain string is the Vertex AI one.
- Gemini-format connections: tool calls without a signature (including those in ST's history) get `skip_thought_signature_validator` when the channel is off, the synthetic turn has no signature for it, or after a fallback. ST only adds it for `gemini-3` model names.
- New `connection.openAiSignatures` switch (off by default): OpenAI-compatible connections also send the built-in signatures, as OpenRouter `reasoning_details` and CLIProxyAPI `extra_content.google.thought_signature`. It stays off so the extra fields never reach endpoints that might reject them.
- Signatures in responses are read in every format (Gemini `thoughtSignature`, `reasoning_details`, `extra_content`), passed back as-is in multi-tool loops, and tool calls returned to ST carry `reasoning_details`.
- **Fallback**: if a request that carried a built-in signature is rejected because of the thought signature, AP retries it once without the signature and suggests switching the channel or turning signatures off.
- `streamToolArguments: auto` now also asks on custom generateContent endpoints and on the Gemini API source behind a reverse proxy, which may end at Vertex AI. AI Studio silently ignores the request.
- Config page: *Thought signature* is now a select (Off / Vertex AI / AI Studio), and there is a new *OR/CPA signatures* switch.

### Preset updates
- New manifest field **`updateUrl`**: copies installed from a file, including preset files that AP took over, check this URL for updates. Must be `http(s)`; root-only (`preset.yaml`).
- **Automatic updates**: at startup AP downloads every installed preset that has an update source (the link it was installed from, or `updateUrl`) and installs it when the version is higher ("Updated to x.y.z"). Trust prompts work as usual, and a build you declined is not offered again. Built-in and dev-server presets are not auto-updated. The Presets page shows *Update from source* for every preset with an update source.
- **AP updates itself for `minAdvancedPreset`**: when a preset needs a newer AP, AP pulls its own update through ST, reloads, and then resumes the install (the artifact is kept in the tab's sessionStorage). This also applies to automatic updates and to taking over preset files. If no update is available, the update fails, or the same update was already tried in this browser session, the install is refused with a hint to update from the Extensions panel.
- When a built-in preset in the extension is newer than a copy you installed yourself (for example a manually installed Petals), AP removes that copy and its update source at startup and switches back to the built-in, with a notice. Copies with the same or a higher version are kept.

### User modules
- Every insertion entry, every build-variable update, and each dict key or list item inside an update can be switched on or off in the editor, so you can compare combinations without deleting anything.
- Switches are part of the module content: they are exported, imported, duplicated and bundled with presets, and they count toward the "you changed this bundled module" comparison. Only `enabled: false` is stored.
- CLI sources (`user-modules/`, `user-module-templates/`): `<!-- @entry point=… enabled=false -->`, and the YAML tag `!off` in `vars` switches off a whole update, a dict key or a list item.
- Editor: dict updates use a stacked key / value layout, and the list row summary skips the parts that are switched off. All editor text fields use the same monospace font.

### Fixes
- Stopped generations now behave like native requests:
  - A request stopped before it is sent rejects without contacting the backend. Tavern Helper's prompt viewer, which starts a generation and stops it at `CHAT_COMPLETION_SETTINGS_READY`, no longer leaves a new reply.
  - A non-streaming request stopped while running rejects instead of being saved as a reply, so script calls such as `generate` get an error, not a partial result.
- Shorter installer hint in the export dialog; "OR/CPA" abbreviation for OpenRouter / CLIProxyAPI in labels.

### Other
- GitHub Release bodies are taken from `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`.
- Docs, the `ap init` template (`updateUrl` hint) and bundled Agent Skills updated.
- **Built-in Petals 7.11.0.**

The artifact format is unchanged (3).
- AP before 1.11.0 ignores `updateUrl`.
- Older AP versions read a channel value of `sendThoughtSignature` as a plain on/off switch and send per-channel `thoughtSignature` objects broken. Presets using them should set `minAdvancedPreset: 1.11.0`; `ap check` warns.
- In user modules, older versions drop switched-off list items but still apply switched-off entries, updates and dict keys.
- Building `!off`, `enabled=false`, channel signatures and `updateUrl` needs CLI 1.11.0.
